questions.q: What is a legal entity, in Oracle Fusion enterprise structure terms?
options: A real, legally registered organization that can sign a contract or owe tax
The segment structure of the chart of accounts
A report that lists open invoices
The accounting book that stores transactions
questions.explain: A legal entity is the legal "who" — a real, registered organization recognized by law.

questions.q: What does a ledger use, by definition, to record a legal entity's transactions?
options: A single cross-validation rule
One chart of accounts, one calendar, and one currency
Any number of charts of accounts chosen per transaction
A business unit's org chart
questions.explain: A ledger is defined by exactly one chart of accounts, one calendar, and one currency, among other accounting options.

questions.q: Which enterprise structure actually processes day-to-day transactions like invoices and sales orders?
options: The chart of accounts
The legal entity
The business unit
The accounting calendar
questions.explain: The business unit is the operational unit that processes transactions and routes accounting entries into a ledger.

questions.q: What happens if a business unit is assigned to the wrong legal entity or ledger?
options: The chart of accounts automatically corrects itself
Oracle Fusion blocks all future transactions permanently
Nothing, business units are purely cosmetic
Every transaction that business unit processes posts to the wrong set of books
questions.explain: Because transactions route through the business unit's assignments, a wrong assignment sends accounting entries to the wrong ledger and books.

questions.q: Why do enterprise structures need to be configured before entering real transactions?
options: Because Oracle requires alphabetical setup order
Because every later course assumes legal entities, ledgers, business units, and a chart of accounts already exist and are correctly assigned
Because transactions can be entered without any business unit
Because chart of accounts segments do not affect transactions
questions.explain: You cannot post an invoice without a business unit, run a business unit without a ledger, or have a ledger without a chart of accounts — structure is the foundation transactions are poured onto.
